target_customer: K-12 schools and districts that pay for software to track student behavior and social emotional needs
problem: Schools learn about student behavior and emotional problems late and scattered across staff, so interventions come after problems escalate.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription sold to schools and districts
product_category: Student behavior and social emotional learning software

founders.name: Julian Golder
founders.background_notes: YC page says he opened and ran a school focused on deep differentiation, developed a national curriculum and was an early hire at Wyzant. The Unreasonable Group page says he spent 12 years in education before building the team in 2016.

technical_complexity.rationale: A web platform for collecting observations and showing indicators; the hard parts were school data integrations and privacy compliance, not research. Later AI claims are from current marketing.

defensibility.rationale: Accumulated student history and school workflows create some lock-in, but behavior tracking tools are copyable and school student information systems can add similar modules.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: PowerSchool bought Chalkable (student behavior tools) in October 2016 and Kickboard in 2021 per The Journal, showing incumbents consolidating this wedge; Emote itself was not acquired in sources found.

market_need_then: Schools were adopting behavior and SEL frameworks such as PBIS; the YC page frames the original product as a school wide tool where staff, parents and students share observations. No dated demand figures were found.

identity.logo: A fortune cookie (per the company website)
identity.voice_and_tone: Care focused with the tagline Data that Drives Care and a Care Before Crisis theme

branding.community_and_virality: No sources found for community, merch or press about the brand itself.

brand_strength.rationale: The name is a common word shared with gaming emotes and several unrelated startups, and no source shows brand driven awareness.

outcome_analysis: Emote has stayed small: the YC page lists a team of six and the Unreasonable Group page lists one to five employees, with claims of over 250 schools onboarded per month that are self reported and undated. No funding beyond an unverified aggregator figure was found, so whether it stalled or is a quietly sustainable business cannot be told from public sources.
notes: Funding: CB Insights and BounceWatch (aggregators, seen in search snippets only) report about 120K from Y Combinator in August 2016; unverified so not recorded as a round. An aggregator lists Lei Xu as co-founder but no company source confirms it, so not listed. The Journal 2021 funding story is about EmpowerU, a different company. No competitor source dated near 2016 was found, so the list is empty. The newer product Emote Connect appears on schooldataleadership.org as early access. Name collisions with other companies called Emote are common.
